newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub gas called higher with heat, firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub gas called higher with heat, firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Monday as temperature highs were forecast to flirt with 100 degrees F in many parts of the U.S. this week, sources said.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.11 to $2.125 after settling to the downside Friday at $2.094 per million British thermal units.
Helping to boost futures was early talk of firmer cash prices at $2.17-2.18 at Henry Hub.
"It could exhaust itself pretty quickly though," one trader said, adding he anticipated strong resistance at $2.155.
Further resistance was pegged at $2.24, while support was seen at last week's low of $2.051 and then $2.

Temperatures across the Northeast are expected to reach highs near 100 degrees F over the next couple of days, while above-normal temperatures are also forecast to blanket most of the Midwest, Gulf Coast and Southeast, according to Weather Services Corp said.

However, forecasts for later this week and into early next week are calling for normal to below-normal temperatures throughout most of the eastern half of the U.S., including Texas and the southern plains.

In Friday's cash, Gulf Coast prices edged up one cent to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the low-$2s, while New York city gate gas also was modestly higher near $2.40.
